A NOVEL CASE OF RESTLESS LEG SYNDROME (RLS) DUE TO
INTRACEREBRAL HAEMORRHAGE
B. Chandra1, L. Yeo Leong Litt2. 1General Medicine, Alexandra
Hospital (Jurong Health),2Neurology, National university Hospital,
Singapore, Singapore
Case report: We report a novel case of a 58 year old Chinese female
with restless leg syndrome (RLS), two days after an intracerebral
haemorrhage.
RLS has been described in association with strokes previously in
the literature. This is the ﬁrst description of a clinically typical
symptomatic RLS which occurred secondary to a well-deﬁned
cerebral bleed in the basal ganglia. The diagnosis of RLS was made
using the diagnostic criteria of the International RLS Study Group
(IRLSSG).

We describe her symtpoms and clinical course and reviewed the
current literature of RLS with stroke
Conclusion: We describe this ﬁrst case RLS due to cerebral bleed
and suggest that such cases have a better outcome and quicker
resolution than patients with RLS due to ischemic stroke.

ENDURANCE PERFORMANCE IN ELDERLY WITH DIFFERENT
DEGREES OF KYPHOSIS AS DETERMINED BY THE OCCIPUT-WALL
DISTANCE (OWD)
S. Wongsa, S. Amatachaya, J. Saengsuwan, P. Amatachaya,
T. Thaweewannakij.School of Physical Therapy, Faculty of Associated
Medical Sciences, Khon Kaen University, Khonkaen, Thailand
Background: Kyphosis can be measured using different methods.
The occiput-wall distance (OWD) is one of practical measures
that likely used in epidemiologic studies relating to the kyphosis.
However, only a few evidences on the use of OWD are currently
available. This study compared the endurance performance in
elderly with different degrees of kyphosis as determined by the
OWD.
Methods: Forty three well-functioning elderly were screened the
severity of kyphosis using the OWD [mild (≤5cm), moderate
(5.1–8cm), and severe (<8cm)]. Twenty four subjects were eligible
with the inclusion criteria, 8 subjects in each group. All of them
wereevaluatedenduranceperformanceusingthe6-minutewalking
test (6MinWT). The ﬁndings among the groups were compared
using the one-way ANOVA (p<0.05).
Results: The OWD of subjects were signiﬁcantly different among
the groups (p<0.001). In addition, the results of 6MinWT showed
signiﬁcantly different between subjects with mild and severe
kyphosis (p<0.05).
Conclusions: The ﬁndings conﬁrmed that the OWD can be used as
a practical tool to indicate levels of functional impairments due to
kyphosis.

STIFF PERSON SYNDROME ASSOCIATED WITH AUTOIMMUNE
THYROIDITIS AND SARCOIDOSIS OF INTRATHORACIC LYMPH
NODES: CASE REPORT
Z.A. Zalyalova
1,2, D.M. Khasanova1,2. 1Department of Neurology
and Rehabilitation, Kazan State Medical University,2Republican
Consultative Diagnostical Centre of Movement Disorders and
Botulinitherapy, Kazan, Russia
We represent case report of stiff person syndrome (SPS) with
eyes’ movement disorders and cerebellar symptoms in patient
with veriﬁed autoimmune thyroiditis and conﬁrmed sarcoidosis
of intrathoracic lymph nodes.
The patient P., 50, suffers from signiﬁcant strain, muscle stiffness,
especially in the back, abdomen and pelvic girdle that complicated
gait. Vertical ocular misalignment, limited abduction of the

left eye, rotatory nystagmus. Hyperlordosis in lumbar spine.
Signiﬁcantbilateralbrisktendonreﬂexes.Finger-nosetestcannotbe
performed because of stiffness. Intramuscular electromyography:
Stormy activity of motor unit potentials with signiﬁcant overtone at
the background is registered. Glutamate decarboxylase antibodies =
196U/l, immunoglobulinG=1 6 . 6 8g/l.
From 2004 the diagnosis of autoimmune thyroiditis conﬁrmed by
puncture biopsy. In 2005 the diagnosis of SPS was made out, and
she received diazepam, clonazepam, baclofen, tizanidine, which
gave no relief. In 2008 patient took a course of plasma exchange
without apparent result, then course of immunoglobulins, which
signiﬁcantly worsening the condition. In 2009 – gasping without
physical exercise, severe pain in the chest. X-ray, then pucture
biopsy elicited sarcoidisis of intrathoracic lymph nodes. The course
of steroid therapy was performed with good recovery.
In 2010 botulinotherapy was performed and its effectiveness
was high. After injections the patient marked substantially
improvement: walks by herself. There are no data in medical
literature showing SPS with systemic pathology of cell-immune
answer, i.e. sarcoidosis. Botulinotherapy may be one of the variants
of symptomatic treatment of patients with SPS that can raise the
quality of life of such patients.
1.314
NEUROLOGICAL SYNDROMES ASSOCIATED WITH GLUTAMIC
ACID DECARBOXYLASE ANTIBODIES: A BRAZILIAN SERIES
H.A.G. Teive1, M. Fernandes1, A.M. Ferreira1, W.O. Arruda1,
P. Lorenzoni1, R.P. Munhoz1, P. Carrilho2. 1Neurology Service, Internal
Medicine Department, Hospital de Clinicas, Federal University of
Paran´a, Curitiba,
2Neurology, Clinica Neurologica, Cascavel, Brazil
Introduction: Glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies(Anti-GAD)
associated neurological disorders includes Stiff-person syndrome,
and its variants, such as stiff-trunk syndrome, stiff-limb syndrome,
progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus and
SPS-plus. Cerebellar ataxia and epilepsy are also associated to anti-
GAD syndromes.
Objective: To describe neurological disorders associated with anti-
GAD in a Brazilian series of 12 patients.
Patients and Methods: This Brazilian series includes 12 patients
with neurological disorders associated with Anti-GAD (Laboratory-
supported – RIA) or electromyographic (EMG) ﬁndings (continuous
motor unit activity). Seven patients were females and ﬁve patients
were males and mean age of diagnosis was 47.25 years.
Results: This series includes 5 cases of stiff-limb syndrome (2
cases with stiff-lower limbs, 2 cases with stiff-one limb, one case
with stiff-three-limbs), 4 cases of classical stiff-person syndrome
and 3 cases of ataxia cerebellar associated with anti-GAD. Apart
from one patient, all had positive serum serology for anti-GAD.
All patients with stiff-person and stiff-limb syndrome had EMG
conﬁrmation. Diabetes mellitus (3), Hashimotto thyroiditis (4), and
vitiligo (1) were observed in the present series. Epilepsy was found
in 3 patients.
Conclusion: In this Brazilian series of neurological syndromes
associated with anti-GAD we found 5 cases of stiff-limb syndrome,
4 cases of classical stiff-person syndrome, and 3 cases of cerebellar
ataxia. Epilepsy was associated in three patients.
